items.text: Mountaintop, Riverside Village
The silver thread coils around Chéng's waist and drags him back onto the cliff.
He hits the ground and rolls, the stabbing pain in his left leg catching up to him on impact.
A broken branch is lodged in his calf.
The village doctor stands over him, calmly reeling the silver thread back onto a bone shuttle.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It's you!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Playing the lone hero isn't a healthy habit.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It's how I usually get things done.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Someone had to resolve the matter. Agh. Besides, once I see a problem, I cannot turn a blind eye to it.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I couldn't involve those hunters again, not after they scarcely made it back alive.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: How can you be so sure they wouldn't have lent a hand?
Doctor Xiù steps closer, squatting down and inspecting the wound on his left leg.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Good news: it doesn't appear too deep.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Are you ready?
She doesn't wait for an answer. In one swift motion, she yanks the branch free, and the wound wells with blood.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Tch.
Satisfied there are no splinters left in the wound, Doctor Xiù guides her silver thread through a series of precise sutures.
With practiced ease, she applies herbs pulled from her robes to the wound, then cuts and ties a clean white bandage.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Thank you. You've quite the unique method for treating wounds.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Ah, I just find some joy in experimenting with my arcane skill.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Forgive my bluntness, but what are you doing here, Doctor?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: The Hú family refused to let the hunter stay after I patched him up, so I had him taken to my clinic. Whether he survives or not is in fate's hands now.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: In any case, it struck me that you looked somewhat familiar.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I asked around where you'd gone and was promptly informed that you'd inquired about the tiger's whereabouts and run off alone. To face the beast, no doubt.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: "That can't be!" I told them, but their faces were deadly serious. I was worried something might happen, so I hurried over.
Doctor Xiù falls silent, her eyes lingering on Chéng.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: If not for your lack of familiarity with the terrain, your getting lost notwithstanding, I doubt I'd have been able to catch up to you in time.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It wasn't all that dangerous, although the tiger was fiercer than I had anticipated.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Hah, the recklessness of youth.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: May I know your name?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Chéng Héguāng.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I must say, Chéng Héguāng, that flying-feather technique of yours is quite curious. A skill passed down through your family, I presume?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: That's right.
Doctor Xiù's winding of the bandage falters for an instant before she finishes up and knots it.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I once knew a man by the name of Chéng. He commanded flying metal shards through the air. His abilities were quite impressive.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Still, those who excel in such things tend to have weaker constitutions.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: He used to be on the wrong side of the law, but "official" was written into both his name and his fate. And sure enough, in the end, he became one.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Did you know him?
Chéng clenches his teeth, his focus shifting to the remaining flying feathers on his shoulder.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I can see you've discerned it already. He was my father.
Finished with the bandaging, Doctor Xiù stands up and dusts off her hands.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Oh! Well, that's quite the coincidence!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Your father and I were friends. Which, I suppose, makes you my nephew, or near enough.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: So listen, nephew: this injury will take a few days to heal, and the dressing will need changing. My clinic is at the foot of the mountain. Come stay with me for a few days.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I brought little money with me. I'm afraid I may not have enough to cover the medical expenses for the next few days.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: You think I'm after a few coins? Just stay. You can pay me back by lending me your hand when you can.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Might I lend you mine in getting up?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: No need. I can manage.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: The two set off together down the mountain.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: You seem young. Are you still studying, or have you already become an official?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Neither. I mostly get by on odd jobs.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: And what "odd job" brought you to this poor place in the middle of nowhere?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I was running an errand for someone and happened to pass through.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I see. How is your mother?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Well enough.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Hmm. And your father?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: He passed away.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: What happened?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: He had an accident.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I'm sorry. I never would have imagined.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Imagined?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Mhm. He was still young. But, I suppose death comes for us all.
A long silence falls.
Foot of Mountain, Riverside Village
Reaching the foot of the mountain, they push through the grass and follow the stream for a short distance.
From between the trees, a solitary white house emerges into view.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Why set up a clinic out here in the wilderness? It would be easier to see patients if you lived in the village.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Convenient, sure. But the houses in the village are tall and crammed together one after another. Living like that would be maddening.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: But your clinic has the same black roof tiles and white walls. It looks no different from the houses in Zhu County or the village.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: What do you expect me to do, paint the house black from top to bottom?
Doctor Xiù whirls, sending three silver threads like spider silk toward Chéng's vital joints.
As if he'd anticipated the attack, Chéng dodges. Flying feathers clash with silver threads, tangling as they fall to the ground.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: What was that?!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Ah, you could have stood and taken the threads, yet you chose to dodge and tear the wound open instead.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Your command over your arcane skill is undisciplined, to say the least. Had you used it properly earlier, you'd have subdued the tiger without so much as a scratch.
Doctor Xiù shakes her head and sighs.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I remember how your father would turn leaves to metal, sending them flying as he bid. There are plenty of leaves here. Why not give it a try?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I can't.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Everyone from my clan can control light metals, but transmutation ... I am the only one left who can do it. Or at least, I ought to be.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: You've chosen not to use this unique ability?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Not exactly.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I can no longer control it, as if something is blocking me. As a child, I used it recklessly. It caused an accident. After that, with no one to guide me, I dared not use it often.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: A waste, if you ask me. Only you possess this ability, and yet you shackle yourself with hesitation.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Your father and I sparred many times, enough for me to become familiar with his arcane skill.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: His arcane skill, like mine, relied on guiding matter with Qi. If you wish it, I can teach you a few techniques. Be a guide of sorts.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: But why?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Why? Because I want to, and because it's the right thing to do.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Chéng Héguāng, when an elder offers you her teachings, you shut your mouth and listen.
Main Room, Clinic
Doctor Xiù swings open the clinic door without ceremony.
Inside the clinic, an assistant is busy boiling medicine. Two or three patients lie resting nearby, including the hunter whose arm was mauled earlier.

items.speaker: Assistant
items.text: Doctor, you're back! Who's this?

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: A patient I picked up on the road. How's the hunter?

items.speaker: Assistant
items.text: He's still unconscious.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Alright. Be sure to change his dressing in a couple of hours and keep a close eye on him tonight. A fever could prove fatal.
One of the patients, a young man, hops out of bed and runs over, his face flushed with color.

items.speaker: Young Man
items.text: Doctor! That medicine's incredible! I've never felt so alive, like I could plow two acres of land without so much as a breath!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I'm glad to hear—

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: Doctor! Help! Help!
Doctor Xiù lets out a weary sigh and walks over to the old man's bed.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: What is it this time?

items.speaker: Old Man
items.text: I still feel terribly ill. My stomach hurts, and I throw up every time I eat.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I gave you strict instructions not to have any food! But you just couldn't help yourself, could you?

items.speaker: Assistant
items.text: Uh. I've just brewed him some fresh medicine. I only poured it a moment ago. It's still hot.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: To the assistant's surprise, Doctor Xiù smiles and looks up at Chéng, who is still standing by the door.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Perfect. We have just the man for handling a little heat.
